subject: FinServCo evals: next steps and model recommendations
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver@finservco.com>, Sara Li <sara.li@finservco.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 08 Mar 2027 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: FinServCo evals: next steps and model recommendations

Thanks again for taking time today — great conversation. Quick recap, recommended next steps, and the model/eval approach we discussed so your team can start a lightweight, customer-specific benchmark on Redwood.

Recap (what we heard)
- Primary use case: invoice classification + extraction and templated reply generation for customer support.
- Key constraints: PII-sensitive data, p95 latency target ~200ms, budget sensitivity for high throughput.
- Success criteria you mentioned: extraction accuracy >= 92% (entity-level F1 for amounts/dates), reply quality judged by human eval >= 4/5 on a 5-point scale.

Model recommendations (initial shortlist)
- rw-instruct-7b-q4 (recommended for latency-sensitive workloads; strong instruction-following with quantized footprint)
- rw-rlhf-13b (higher quality for complex extraction & reasoning; higher cost/latency)
- Mistral-Instruct-7B (alternate open checkpoint with good generation quality)

Benchmarks / baseline links
- Our internal finserv benchmark: https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/finserv-bench-2027
- Eval runner docs: https://redwood.ai/docs/evals-runner (instructions + example configs)

Dataset format (recommended)
- CSV or JSONL with the following columns/fields: id, prompt/input, reference/expected_output, split (train/val/test), and optional metadata (source_document_id, pii_tags).
- For extraction tasks use a reference format that encodes entities as JSON in the expected_output field (e.g., {"amount": "$1,234.56", "date": "2027-02-15"}).
- We recommend starting with ~200-500 labeled examples for an initial pass and scaling to 2k+ for robust estimates.

Scoring criteria (suggested)
- Structured extraction: entity-level F1 (span matching + normalized value equality for amounts/dates).
- Classification: accuracy + macro-F1 by class.
- Free-text generation: automated metrics (ROUGE/L, BLEU as signal) + human preference scoring on a 200-sample subset.
- Regression monitoring: compare model output distribution to baseline; alert on >2% absolute drop in primary metric.

Operational notes for running on Redwood
- Upload data (S3 or direct console upload), create an eval job in the Console or via the API, choose model variants (quantized vs full), select metrics, and run against test split.
- We will provision a temporary evaluation project for FinServCo so you can run 3 models in parallel.
- Attachments: evaluation_guidelines.pdf (detailed scoring + human eval template), sample_prompts.csv (example rows).

Next steps / asks
1) Please share a de-identified sample of ~200 labeled examples (CSV or JSONL). If you need, our team can help with a quick de-id pass.
2) Confirm whether you want to prioritize latency (rw-instruct-7b-q4) or precision (rw-rlhf-13b) for the first pass.
3) I'll loop in Neha (SE) to provide a runbook and schedule a 30-min hands-on session for the team to run the first eval.

I'll follow up with the Console project invite and the scripts.

Best,
Marissa
Director, Solutions 
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: FinServCo evals: next steps and model recommendations

Hi Oliver — quick answers and a short runbook to make the first eval frictionless.

1) Preferred reference format
- We prefer a JSONL where expected_output is a JSON string per line for structured extraction. Example row: {"id": "inv_001", "prompt": "Invoice text here...", "reference": "{\"amount\": \"$1,234.56\", \"date\": \"2027-02-15\"}", "split": "test"}.
- JSONL is easiest for nested references and is supported by the Console and the API. CSV is fine for simple classification tasks.

2) PII / de-id
- Keep amounts/dates if they are evaluation targets. Replace names/emails/customer IDs with stable pseudonyms (e.g., CUST_001) so span positions are preserved.
- If you need, we can run a quick de-id script on your files; send a sample and we’ll return a de-identified copy.

3) DPA & security
- We can accept data to the Console under a temporary restricted project after a short intake form. For files with sensitive data we recommend: upload to your S3 bucket with object-level encryption and provide Redwood read-only access. We will not store raw data outside the eval project and will provide deletion instructions. If you need a DPA signed first, that’s fine — our legal team can expedite.

4) How to run an eval (quick runbook)
- Step A: Prepare JSONL (id, prompt, reference, split). Attach sample_prompts.csv for format examples.
- Step B: Upload to S3 or Console (we’ll provide an upload URL / project invite).
- Step C: Create eval job in Console or via API: choose models (rw-instruct-7b-q4, rw-rlhf-13b, mistral-instruct-7b), select metrics (entity_f1, accuracy, rouge_l), set sampling = deterministic, and set batch_size = 8 for faster throughput.
- Step D: Run on the test split. Export results (CSV + JSONL with predictions) and run human review on the 200-sample subset.

5) Scoring specifics we recommend
- Amounts: normalize currency formatting then exact-match on numeric value; treat small rounding differences as equal within 0.5%.
- Dates: normalize to ISO and exact-match.
- Entities: span-level F1 with lenient overlap (>=50% overlap counts).
- Replies: run automated metrics (ROUGE-L) and a human Likert rating for quality/accuracy.

Regression monitoring
- Baseline: record the top metric from the initial run.
- Alert threshold: 2% absolute drop in the primary metric (entity F1) triggers automatic rerun and triage.

Attachments included: sample_prompts.csv (small example), evaluation_guidelines.pdf (human eval template + scoring details).

If you confirm we’ll create the project and send an S3 upload URL. Happy to hop on a 30-min screen share this week to do the upload together.

Best,
Neha
Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
